newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia police warn on poisoning threat.
newsitem.headline: Australia police warn on poisoning threat.

text.p: Australian police on Monday warned shoppers to be vigilant as the deadline in the country's poisoned biscuit extortion threat arrived.
An extortionist has threatened to plant poison-laced biscuits on supermarket shelves along Australia's east coast from Monday.
"Today is the deadline," said a police spokeswoman.
"Retailers and consumers should remain vigilant, and if they suspect packaged food has been tampered with or they notice a strange taste, should contact police immediately."

Packets of Arnotts brand biscuits laced with a pesticide and containing an extortion letter were sent to Arnotts, politicians and a newspaper on February 3. The letter threatened to plant poisoned biscuits in stores in the states of New South Wales and Queensland as of Monday, February 17.

The extortionist has demanded police involved in a 1991 murder case take a lie detector test in an attempt to prove the innocence of a friend now serving a life sentence for the execution-style murder of a bookmaker.
